prompt: Stage 5-1, level 8, 44 gold, 36 HP, six players left. Ezreal is 1-star with three items and you hold a second copy. Your scout: Seat 2 has a 2-star Ezreal and a spare on the bench, Seat 5 has one on the board, nobody else has any. Roughly twenty other 4-cost copies are out across the lobby. Before you roll: how likely is one shop to show an Ezreal, and what does 44 gold buy?

lobby.note: 2-star Ezreal on the board and a spare on the bench

options.label: About one shop in 25: three of ten Ezreal are left in a 4-cost pool of about 115, so 22 shops are roughly a coin flip for one copy
About one shop in three: at level 8 a slot is a 4-cost 30% of the time and Ezreal is the one you are looking for
About one shop in ten, the same as any 4-cost at 8; contest changes who buys the copies, not the odds
Zero: Seat 2 alone holds four, so the last copies are as good as gone and rolling is pointless

explanation:
Count before you roll. Ten Ezreal exist: you hold two, Seat 2 four, Seat 5 one. Seven out, three left. The tier has fourteen 4-costs at ten copies, 140 in all; with your seven and about twenty other copies out, roughly 113 remain. A slot is a 4-cost 30% of the time and an Ezreal 3 of 113 of those: about 0.8% per slot, 4% per five-slot shop, one shop in 25. Forty-four gold is 22 shops, and 22 shots at 4% land at least once about 58% of the time.

The 30% figure is the tier, not your unit, and it is the number that sends players 40 gold into a dead pool. One in ten is right for an untouched pool and wrong here, because seven of ten are already on boards. Zero is also wrong: three copies are three copies, and every one Seat 5 misses is yours. The honest read is a coin flip for one 2-star; the next question is whether that is the best use of 44 gold at 36 HP.
principle: Your odds are the tier odds times your share of the tier's pool; the second number is the one the lobby changes.
commonMistake: Reading '30% four-costs at level 8' as 30% for the four-cost you want.
hint: Add up every Ezreal you can see on boards and benches, including your own, before you touch the odds table.
